set.descent_text: This single pitch ends at the same ledge where the first pitch of Stanley-Burgner ends, so there is no summit descent from it alone. Most parties either rappel the pitch from gear or link into the second pitch of Stanley-Burgner and carry on to the summit. From the summit, walk east a short way and rappel the north face on slung stations, using one rope or two. Then scramble back around to the base of the south face.
set.approach: The Stuart Lake trailhead sits at the end of Forest Road 7601 above Leavenworth. Follow the Stuart Lake Trail (#1599) for about 2.5 miles to the signed junction, bear left onto the Colchuck Lake Trail (#1599A), cross Mountaineer Creek and climb to Colchuck Lake, then work around the shore to the boulder field at its south end. From there Aasgard Pass climbs nearly 2,000 ft of loose scree; it holds snow into early July and has a hidden creek under the slope, so carry an axe early in the season. From the pass, travel cross-country through the Core past Isolation and Tranquil lakes toward Gnome Tarn, the usual bivy about 20 minutes from the south face of Prusik Peak. The pitch starts on the south face about 20 ft left of the usual start of Stanley-Burgner, at the foot of a clean finger crack.

review.notes: MP route page: location 20 ft left of Stanley-Burgner start, tops out at SB P1 exit. MP Stanley-Burgner: walk east from summit, rappel north face on slung stations, 1 or 2 ropes. WTA pages: trail numbers, Aasgard gain/snow hazard. Gnome Tarn bivy distance from MP Der Sportsman sibling research context.

set.descent_text: The last pitch ends on easier ground on the west side of the sail-shaped headwall. From there the Solid Gold rappel anchors are close by. Make two rappels from those anchors, then walk off down the back (north) side and scramble around to the base of the south face.

review.notes: MP: headwall crack spirals to west side to easier ground, aim for Solid Gold rappel anchors; two-rappel count and walk-off kept from the existing row text.

set.approach: Park along Forest Road 9070 where it meets the Pacific Crest Trail at a saddle (about 3,800 ft), roughly six miles from Hyak. Walk the PCT south for about 1.7 miles to a cairned side trail that doubles back uphill; a tarn on your left means you overshot it. The side path climbs about 0.3 mile with a few class 2-3 moves to Abiel Pass, the saddle between Tinkham and Silver peaks, where the scramble up the summit slopes begins.
set.descent_text: Reverse the route: from the summit, follow the path back down the steep rocky upper section to the flat stretch, then to Abiel Pass, and descend the cairned side trail to the PCT. Turn north on the PCT for the walk back to the road. The rock is loose in many places, so descend carefully and keep clear of other parties below.

review.notes: WTA: trailhead, PCT 1.7 mi, side trail to Abiel Pass, class 2 scrambling, loose rock on descent. Assumes standard scramble is this common route.
